caveats: Hallmark sets overlap in membership (e.g. multiple inflammatory sets share genes), so significant sets are correlated findings, not independent discoveries — say so before reporting a count
Row z-scaling makes every pathway look like it has range; the colour scale is not evidence of effect size, the score difference is
If sample_01 sits in the inflamed group, its removal leaves 5 vs 6 and further reduces power — report the sensitivity result as a stability check, not a replacement analysis
steps.context: This is the step that answers the user's actual question. With 6 vs 6 the analysis is underpowered for anything but large, coherent effects — in inflamed UC colon the expectation is strong inflammatory hallmarks (TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB, INFLAMMATORY_RESPONSE, INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE, IL6_JAK_STAT3_SIGNALING, COMPLEMENT) — but the analysis must report what the data show, including null results, and must not be steered toward that expectation. Testing GSVA scores with limma is standard practice but is known to be anti-conservative because the scores are derived from the same samples; that limitation must be stated.
steps.question: Which hallmark pathways separate ulcerative colitis inflamed from control colon samples, and is the separation robust to the low-depth sample_01?
constraints: Use the exact condition labels from metadata.csv in all figure legends and tables — do not relabel as 'treated/control' generically
Report BH-adjusted p-values as the primary inference; nominal p-values may be shown but must be labelled as exploratory
Do not claim a pathway 'separates' the groups on the basis of heatmap clustering alone — clustering must be corroborated by the differential test
steps.description: Take the 50 x 12 hallmark GSVA score matrix from T1S2 and (a) test each hallmark for a difference between the inflamed and control groups using limma on the score matrix with design ~condition, reporting moderated t, log-scale score difference (mean inflamed - mean control), raw p and BH-adjusted p for every set, sorted by adjusted p; (b) draw the requested heatmap — hallmark sets as rows, the 12 samples as columns, scores row-scaled (z-score across samples), with a column annotation bar for condition from metadata.csv and a second annotation for library size, hierarchical clustering of both rows and columns, using ComplexHeatmap or pheatmap. Produce both a full 50-set heatmap and a focused heatmap of the top ~15 sets by adjusted p. Also produce a PCA of samples in hallmark-score space and a per-pathway boxplot/strip panel (inflamed vs control) for the top sets. Sensitivity: repeat the differential test with sample_01 removed (5 inflamed or 5 control as appropriate) and report which hallmarks change significance status, so that any result driven by that single low-depth library is identified. Summarise in plain text which pathways separate the groups, with effect size and adjusted p, and which do not survive the sensitivity check.
acceptance_criteria: A results table covering every retained hallmark set with mean score per group, difference, moderated t, raw p and BH-adjusted p is written and the top sets are named in the summary
A row-scaled hallmark-by-sample heatmap with a condition annotation bar and clustered rows and columns is produced (full 50-set and top-set versions)
The leave-one-out re-run excluding sample_01 is reported, naming any hallmark whose significance status changes
The written summary states the number of hallmarks passing BH < 0.05 and explicitly reports if that number is zero rather than falling back to nominal p-values as if they were significant
The summary states that limma on GSVA scores is anti-conservative (scores are derived from the same 12 samples) and that n=6 per group limits the detectable effect size

plan.title: UC inflamed vs control hallmark GSVA sample scores
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question asks for a per-sample pathway activity score and a hallmark heatmap that shows which pathways separate ulcerative colitis inflamed colon from control. The input is a 12,000 x 12 raw Salmon gene-level count matrix (counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column) with a 12-row metadata table giving condition for 6 inflamed vs 6 control samples, unpaired, single batch. Human hallmark gene sets (50 sets, HGNC symbols) are staged in the reference store, so the sample-level scoring the question asks for is directly feasible.

The flow is three steps. T1S1 prepares the expression matrix: library-size QC (the profile flags sample_01 at ~4x below median library size, which is exactly the kind of depth artefact that shows up as a spurious sample-level pathway score), low-count filtering, and a variance-stabilising transformation (DESeq2 VST) that puts samples on a comparable, homoscedastic scale — the required input for GSVA, which is sensitive to depth-driven scale differences. It also resolves duplicate gene symbols, since GMT matching is symbol-based. T1S2 runs GSVA on the 50 hallmark sets to produce the per-sample score matrix the user asked for, and T1S3 tests each hallmark score for a difference between inflamed and control (moderated t-test via limma on the score matrix, BH-adjusted) and draws the annotated heatmap plus a sample-level PCA/correlation view, so that 'which pathways separate the groups' is answered by a statistic, not just by visual clustering.

Two rigor constraints are built in. First, with n=6 per group, GSVA scores are relative to the sample set — they are not absolute activity, and the differential test on them is anti-conservative relative to a gene-level competitive test; the steps must state this. Second, sample_01's low depth must be reported alongside its scores and its influence checked by a leave-one-out re-run, so that any 'separating' pathway driven by that one library is not reported as biology.
